Its annotation describes a punitive 'cure' path (20% charge), which is diametrically opposed to the remedy described in bgb_505 for the same obligation type. This node creates the other side of the core conflict. Its annotation mandates a penalty-free cure path, directly contradicting bgb_491. Furthermore, it explicitly carves out exceptions from the main consumer loan rules, making it a critical point of divergence and incompatibility.

This record broadly applies the consumer loan framework to other financing types, effectively propagating the instability from the core conflict into related legal areas. Its many outbound references make it a multiplier of the initial risk.
